SourceActivities: 13.1 Left to Right semaphore rotation description
13.2 Turning on a Grid four angle/centre scenarios

Task.Prompt: Draw and label three stages mapping original asymmetric triangle ABC by translation, 90-degree rotation about D and reflection across x=3; justify centre, direction, angle and congruence. Also show 90-degree clockwise and 180-degree rotations of a quadrilateral on a grid.

Criteria.Criterion: states correct centre, direction and angle for every requested rotation
constructs and labels accurate quarter-turn, half-turn and other nonzero grid rotations
records all three intermediate triangle images in translation/rotation/reflection order
explains matched vertices, preserved distances and angle measures

Practice.Prompt: What three parameters specify a rotation?
A flag arm from (0,0) to (2,0) turns 90 counterclockwise. Where does its tip land?
Translate quadrilateral vertices using v=(2,-1). What changes?
Practice.Expected: Each point adds (2,-1); no side or angle measure changes.

Practice.Prompt: Which points stay fixed when reflected over line y=0?
Practice.Expected: All points on y=0 and only those points.

Practice.Prompt: How do you locate a point equally distant from three non-collinear sites?
Practice.Expected: Intersection of two perpendicular bisectors of their joining segments.

Practice.Prompt: Why do equal-circle-radius lengths imply a rhombus in two-circle construction?
Practice.Expected: All four sides joining the two centres to the two intersections have the common radius.

FirstPartyCooldown: EDULYTIKS_AUTHORED_COOLDOWN: rotate point P=(2,1) 90 degrees CCW about O=(0,0), giving (-1,2), explain radius and directed angle
PaperDelivery: Student gives labelled paper rotation/translation/reflection stages and protractor justifications to teacher; teacher marks 0/1/2 per criterion, signs/date feedback offline.

Cases.CORRECT: centre, angle/direction and all intermediate images correctly identified
Cases.EQUIVALENT: different valid congruent target image with explicitly redefined final D,E,F and all three rigid stages
Cases.WRONG: clockwise confused with counterclockwise or original image relabelled without moving points
Cases.INSUFFICIENT: one final sketch without intermediate vertices or reasoning
Cases.MALFORMED: unspecified rotation centre, target or direction
